title: Optimization of 6-Layer All-Dielectric Polarizing Beam Splitter
scientific_hypothesis: A 6-layer stack utilizing high-index contrast materials (TiO2/SiO2 or Ta2O5/SiO2) can achieve mean TE reflectance >90% and mean TM transmittance >85% at 45 degrees incidence across 500-650 nm by leveraging destructive interference for TM polarization and constructive reflection for TE polarization within the limited degrees of freedom.
design_principle: Maximize refractive index contrast between adjacent layers to enhance polarization selectivity. Use a symmetric or near-symmetric structure to manage phase accumulation. Optimize thicknesses to create a 'polarization-dependent bandgap' where TE is reflected and TM is transmitted.
proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
manufacturing_considerations: High-index TiO2 may require precise stoichiometry control
Low total layer count simplifies fabrication but reduces spectral bandwidth control
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for polarizing beam splitters
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for planar multilayer systems
Refractive index dispersion data for TiO2 and SiO2 in visible spectrum
expected_advantages: Simplest structure with lowest material cost and deposition time
Potentially highest robustness due to fewer interfaces and thinner total stack
known_risks: Limited degrees of freedom may prevent simultaneous satisfaction of both TE R and TM T targets across the full 150 nm bandwidth
Sensitivity to thickness errors may be higher due to narrower operational bandwidth
execution_request_english: Perform a numerical optimization of a 6-layer all-dielectric polarizing beam splitter on a fused silica substrate. Incident medium: Air. Substrate: Fused Silica. Incidence angle: 45 degrees. Wavelength range: 500-650 nm. Materials: TiO2 and SiO2 for the coating layers. Stack sequence: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Design variables: Thicknesses of all 6 coating layers, bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm. Objective: Maximize a composite score that rewards Mean TE Reflectance (target >= 90%) and Mean TM Transmittance (target >= 85%), while penalizing total physical thickness. After finding the optimal thicknesses, perform a robustness analysis by simulating the response with independent normally distributed layer-thickness errors (sigma = 1.5% of nominal thickness) and a common incidence-angle offset uniformly distributed between -1 and +1 degree. Report the optimal thicknesses, the mean TE reflectance, mean TM transmittance, total thickness, and the statistical distribution of performance under uncertainty. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 45 degrees. polarization s, p. wavelength intervals 500-650 nm. soft objectives: high TE reflectance (mean >= 90%); high TM transmittance (mean >= 85%); fewer layers; lower total thickness. robustness conditions: layer thicknesses bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm; total layer counts restricted to 6, 10, or 14.
